title: L-band single-photon generation from a cavity-coupled silicon C-center
authors: Carolina Crosta, Kyu-Young Kim, Purbita Purkayastha, Abhijit Biswas, Jasvith Raj Basani, Amirehsan Alizadehherfati, Amirehsan Boreiri, Chang-Min Lee, Fabio Pezzoli, Edo Waks
abstract: Monolithic integration of single-photon sources into silicon photonics offers a compelling solution for realizing scalable quantum telecommunication architectures. Among the candidate silicon color centers, the C-center features a zero-phonon emission in the telecom L-band, corresponding to the spectral window of minimum transmission loss in optical fibers. Despite this advantage, isolating single C-centers has remained an unrealized challenge in solid-state quantum optics. In this work, we report the isolation of a single silicon C-center. We enhance the spontaneous emission rate of the zero-phonon line by coupling the single emitter to a nanophotonic crystal cavity, observing a fivefold reduction in the excited-state lifetime compared to bulk conditions, which corresponds to a Purcell factor lower bound of 33. Second-order autocorrelation measurements confirm single-photon emission from the investigated defect, obtaining an optical purity of $g^{(2)}(0) = 0.23$ without background correction. Our results establish a native telecom L-band quantum light source in silicon, laying the foundation for ultra-low-loss and long-distance quantum applications.
summary: This paper reports the successful realization of a single, high-performance quantum light source using a silicon C-center defect coupled to a photonic crystal cavity. By demonstrating strong Purcell enhancement and confirming single-photon emission in the telecom L-band, the research establishes a critical building block for future low-loss quantum communication technologies.
main_problem: The primary goal is to create a scalable, low-loss, and long-distance quantum light source using single-photon emitters integrated into silicon photonics.
main_result: The authors successfully isolated a single silicon C-center and demonstrated single-photon emission ($g^{(2)}(0) = 0.23$) with a significant Purcell enhancement ($F_P \geq 33$) in the telecom L-band.
method: The study combines advanced optical characterization techniques, including time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) measurements and second-order autocorrelation measurements, on a solid-state platform.
model_or_system: The system utilizes a single C-center defect in Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) coupled to a high-quality factor nanophotonic crystal cavity. The physics is analyzed using concepts from cavity quantum electrodynamics (Purcell effect) and single-photon statistics.
key_observables: Zero-phonon line (ZPL) emission at $\sim 1570$ nm, excited-state lifetime ($	au$), Purcell factor ($F_P$), and the second-order correlation function $g^{(2)}(0)$.
important_parameters: Telecom L-band (1565 - 1625 nm), Purcell factor lower bound of 33, and $g^{(2)}(0) = 0.23$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the observed enhancement is due to cavity coupling, and the single-photon nature is confirmed by $g^{(2)}(0) < 0.5$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the PL spectrum vs. detuning, time-resolved PL showing lifetime changes, and the $g^{(2)}(	au)$ measurement confirming single-photon statistics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical system (C-center in SOI) to demonstrating cavity coupling via PL enhancement, quantifying the enhancement via lifetime measurements (Purcell factor), and finally confirming single-photon emission using $g^{(2)}$ measurements.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering challenge of integrating quantum emitters into silicon photonics, which is a cornerstone technology for scalable quantum networks and quantum communication.

figures.caption: Figure 1: a) Atomic structure of the C-center. Black, orange and red spheres represent silicon, oxygen and car- bon atoms respectively; b) Electronic structure of the C- center with transition wavelengths at cryogenic tempera- tures; c) SEM image of the nanophotonic crystal cavity; d) Schematic of the experimental configuration. The emit- ter is excited from top, while the emitted light is collected in-plane through a lensed single-mode fiber.

Figure 2: a) Reflectivity spectrum of the cavity tuned at the C0-line wavelength (dots) and corresponding Lorentzian fit (dashed line), extracting FWHM = 0.11 ± 0.02 nm that corresponds to a quality factor of (1.4 ± 0.3) × 104; b) Pho- toluminescence spectrum (dots) of the emitter at 8 K un- der 800 nm CW excitation, pump power of 10 µW, in on- resonance condition. The Lorentzian fit of the experimental data (dashed line) provides λZPL = 1569.831±0.004 nm and FWHM = 0.078±0.001 nm; c) Photoluminescence intensity as a function of the cavity mode detuning δ. The dashed line is a visual guide to follow the change of δ.

Figure 4: a) On-resonance C-center count rate as a func- tion of 800 nm CW pump power (dots) and two-level system fit (solid line) with Equation 2, extracting Psat = 10.4±0.3 µW and Isat = (7.68 ± 0.09) × 103 cps; b) Second-order autocorrelation measurement of a C-center under 7 µW = 0.67Psat at 800 nm CW excitation (dots) and correspond- ing fit (solid line) with Equation 3, extracting g(2)(0) = 0.23 ± 0.01.

Figure 3: Time-resolved photoluminescence measurements of a C-center ensemble in a bare nanobeam (orange curve), providing τ0 = 1.45±0.08 µs and a single C-center in a cavity tuned (i) on-resonance (δ = 0 nm, τon = 0.287 ± 0.002 µs); (ii) slightly off-resonance (δ = −0.09 nm, showing a fast increase of the lifetime to τ = 0.523 ± 0.005 µs); and (iii) off-resonance (δ = −0.83 nm, τoff = 0.780 ± 0.030 µs). The C-center is measured at 8 K and excited by a 780 nm pulsed laser with a repetition rate of 100 kHz.
